A1.justification: Both complete 22-page PDFs describe Olympus and contain matching main sections and appendices A–G. Text comparison and visual inspection, including v1's rasterized Figure 4, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original routing and multimodal benchmark results, evaluation on 200 human-generated instructions, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results, including single-task and chain-of-action routing, human-instruction evaluation, and the appendix's model-size and prompt-design ablations.

M1.justification: The model architecture, task-specific routing tokens, specialist models, chain-of-action procedure, training objective and inference process remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices C–D.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OlympusInstruct/OlympusBench task coverage across images, videos and 3D, the same 11 multimodal benchmarks, and the same human-instruction evaluation. Appendix examples retain the same task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: routing and human evaluations retain HuggingGPT with GPT-4o mini and GPT-4o, while Tables 1 and 11 retain their multimodal-model baselines.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, evaluation metrics, sample counts and testing procedures are unchanged. Adding 'jointly' and 'both' to Section 4.1 clarifies combined-dataset fine-tuning already described in v1 and Appendix B. The final experimental prompt in Figure 9 is unchanged.

E4.justification: Task-count, model-size, response-design, prompt-component and instruction-complexity ablations are retained, as are the qualitative examples. Table 11's corrected caption identifies the model comparison already present and discussed in Appendix F; it does not change the analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Results retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Reported scores and qualitative results are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Examples include 94.75% single-task accuracy in Table 2, 91.82% chain-of-action precision in Table 3, and 86.5% human-evaluation success in Table 4.

T1.justification: Equation 1's next-token probability factorization and its variable definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or other mathematical developments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about universal task routing, the two instruction datasets, 20-task coverage and chain-of-action capability, with identical headline performance claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of task-count effects, training costs, model-size differences and prompt-design ablations are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning the quality, diversity and biases of GPT-4o-generated training data.

D1.justification: The front-page project link changes from a GitHub address to an author-hosted project website, revising the supplied access information. Hardware, hyperparameters and implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any change in actual code or data availability.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to HuggingGPT and unified multimodal models remain unchanged. Removing the misplaced citation from Table 11's caption changes a reference backlink, but removes no work from the bibliography or research discussion.

P1.justification: Local edits clarify joint fine-tuning, correct 'Imgae' to 'Image' in Table 8, repair Table 11's caption and slightly rephrase an illustrative instruction in Figure 4. Section organization and the broader narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 changes from a raster image to sharper, selectable text, and Figure 9 receives minor typography adjustments. Table 11's caption is corrected from a task-count ablation description to a comparison of different MLLMs, causing slight page reflow. The figure and table set is retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting Table 11's misleading caption makes it agree with the existing model comparison, while Figure 4's improved rendering and text accessibility make the prompt easier to use. These provide a limited improvement in clarity and presentation; the scientific evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
